notes:
User is planning a weekend garage cleanout and organization project, focusing first on purging and categorizing clutter such as tools, sports equipment, old furniture, storage bins, and boxes. They are motivated and positive about the project.

Garage plans and preferences:
- Apply the “one-touch rule”: once an item is picked up, immediately keep, donate/sell, recycle, or discard it rather than putting it back or moving it elsewhere.
- Use categories such as Keep, Donate/Sell, and Discard; they also considered a temporary “maybe” box with a firm review deadline.
- Group similar items, assign each category a specific home, and keep frequently used supplies accessible; store seasonal/infrequent items higher or farther back.
- Consider shelving, hooks, and a “launching pad” for frequently used items.
- Use sturdy, reinforced, durable, easy-to-clean stackable bins in a variety of sizes. Measure spaces first, ensure stacks are stable, and use clear bins where visibility helps.
- Use concise, bold, consistent labels and possibly color coding. Label both bins and shelf locations. They chose the Brother P-Touch label maker, likely wanting durable labels suitable for a dusty/moisture-prone garage.
- Remove an old desk unused for years and ready to let go; may donate, sell, or responsibly dispose of it.
- Replace the desk footprint with a dedicated workstation for the daily tidying routine, moving work currently done on the kitchen counter. Planned supplies: all-purpose cleaner, disinfectant, dusters, paper towels, cordless vacuum, and microfiber mop.

Bookshelf organization plans:
- Purge damaged, irrelevant, or unwanted books for donation/recycling.
- Group books by category, such as fiction, nonfiction, biographies, or self-help; within categories, organize by author, title, or series.
- Frequently read books should be at eye level or near the front.
- Consider a dedicated “to-read” section.
- Use vertical space with bookends, risers, or stackable shelves; face out favorite books and leave some breathing room.
- Label shelf sections rather than individual books, using clear, consistent labels and the P-Touch.
- Regularly dust and tidy the bookshelf.

Cleaning-supply organization:
- User is deciding between organizing supplies by room or by product type.
- Potential approach: organize primarily by type (all-purpose cleaners, glass cleaners, disinfectants, etc.), then subgroup by room, combining efficient product comparison/reduced duplication with room-based retrieval.
- Store products in a ventilated area away from children and pets; use a caddy or divided bucket for portable organization.
- Label categories and room sections clearly. Keep frequently used products easy to reach and less-used products on higher/harder-to-reach shelves.
- A useful cleanup consideration is reducing duplicate products.

Cleaning routine and preferences:
- User has maintained a daily tidying routine for four weeks (up from the previously noted three weeks) and reports that it has made a remarkable positive difference in the apartment. This is a major accomplishment and source of motivation/pride.
- They plan to incorporate the one-touch rule into the garage cleanout and existing cleaning routine. Advice previously discussed: start small, make immediate deliberate decisions, assign every item a home, attach the rule to an existing habit, practice mindfully, be forgiving after misses, and celebrate small wins.
- Recently started using an all-natural cleaning brand for the bathroom and likes its performance against soap scum and mildew.
